overview.main_topic: Two directions of interoperability (subclassed inside Functional, Functional inside subclassed) and the recommendation to prefer the Functional API
overview.central_idea: Listing 7.15 completes a subclassed Classifier and drops it into a Functional model like any layer. summary:
The page opens with the rest of **Listing 7.15** (started on p.228). The `Classifier(keras.Model)` constructor picks its output head from `num_classes`. With 2 classes it uses **1 unit with a sigmoid** (binary classification). Otherwise it uses **`num_classes` units with a softmax**. It stores the result as `self.dense = layers.Dense(num_units, activation=activation)`, and `call()` just returns `self.dense(inputs)`. The class is then used inside a **Functional** model: `keras.Input(shape=(3,))` → `layers.Dense(64, activation="relu")` → `Classifier(num_classes=10)` → `keras.Model(inputs=inputs, outputs=outputs)`. The subclassed model is called on a symbolic tensor exactly as a built-in layer would be.

"Inversely, you can use a Functional model as part of a subclassed layer or model." **Listing 7.16** first builds a tiny Functional model, `binary_classifier`, that maps a `(64,)` input to one sigmoid unit. It then defines `MyModel(keras.Model)`, which creates `self.dense = layers.Dense(64, activation="relu")` and stores `self.classifier = binary_classifier` in `__init__`, and chains them in `call()`. `model = MyModel()` instantiates it. Weights are created on the first call.

Section **7.2.5, "Remember: Use the right tool for the job,"** wraps up the model-building spectrum from Sequential, the simplest, to subclassing, the most advanced. Each has pros and cons. In general **the Functional API offers a good trade-off between ease of use and flexibility** and gives **direct access to layer connectivity**, which helps with model plotting and feature extraction. The rule: *if you can* use the Functional API, meaning the model can be expressed as a directed acyclic graph of layers, the authors recommend it over subclassing. The discussion continues on p.230, where the book commits to Functional models with subclassed layers.

paragraphs.what_it_says: Interoperability works in the other direction too: a Functional model can be part of a subclassed layer or model.
paragraphs.what_it_means: A Functional model is itself a Layer, so you can assign it as an attribute in a subclass's __init__ and call it in call(). Keras tracks its weights like any sublayer's.
paragraphs.why_it_matters: With both directions possible you can design each part of a system in whichever style suits it. Listing 7.16 shows how.
paragraphs.technical_idea: Beyond the book: the inner Functional model keeps its own graph, so you can still call binary_classifier.summary() or plot_model(binary_classifier) even though MyModel as a whole is opaque.

concepts.name: Interoperability of model-building styles
concepts.definition: Sequential models, Functional models and subclassed layers or models can be nested inside each other freely.
concepts.intuition: Every piece has the same plug, so any piece fits into any socket.
concepts.technical: All are Layer subclasses: they can be called on symbolic tensors in a Functional graph or assigned as attributes and called inside another class's call().
concepts.significance: You can keep custom logic local while keeping the overall model inspectable, or wrap a reusable Functional sub-network inside custom logic.
concepts.example: Listing 7.15 (Classifier inside a Functional model) and Listing 7.16 (binary_classifier inside MyModel).
concepts.misconception: That models and layers are different kinds of objects that can't be mixed. A Model is a Layer with fit/evaluate/predict added (p.227).

concepts.name: Functional API
concepts.definition: Building models by calling layers on symbolic tensors from keras.Input, producing an explicit graph of layers.
concepts.intuition: A wiring diagram Keras can read.
concepts.technical: It stores nodes and edges, which enables plot_model(), connectivity in summary(), and feature extraction.
concepts.significance: The book's recommended default whenever the model is a DAG of layers.
concepts.example: inputs = keras.Input(shape=(3,)); features = layers.Dense(64, activation="relu")(inputs); outputs = Classifier(num_classes=10)(features)
concepts.misconception: That using a subclassed component disqualifies a model from being Functional. It doesn't; the component becomes one node.

concepts.name: Model subclassing
concepts.definition: Defining a model as a keras.Model subclass with layers in __init__ and the forward pass in call().
concepts.intuition: Writing the model as a program.
concepts.technical: Sublayers, including entire Functional models, are tracked as attributes. Connectivity is defined only by code.
concepts.significance: Use it when the model can't be a DAG of layers. Otherwise the Functional API is preferred.
concepts.misconception: That subclassing should be chosen just because it is 'more advanced'.

concepts.name: Sigmoid vs. softmax output head
concepts.definition: For binary classification, one sigmoid unit outputs P(class 1). For multiclass, num_classes softmax units output a probability distribution.
concepts.intuition: A single yes/no dial vs. a pie chart split among the classes.
concepts.technical: Two-class softmax is mathematically equivalent to a single sigmoid on the logit difference, so 1 sigmoid unit is the leaner choice.
concepts.significance: The Classifier hard-codes this standard choice from num_classes.
concepts.example: Classifier(num_classes=2) → Dense(1, sigmoid); Classifier(num_classes=10) → Dense(10, softmax).
concepts.misconception: That binary classification needs 2 output units.

deeper.title: Decision guide distilled from 7.2
deeper.body:
Inference from the book's recommendations (p.216, p.219, p.228-230):

1. Is the model a plain stack of layers with one input and one output? **Sequential** works.
2. Is it any DAG of layers (multiple inputs/outputs, branches, shared layers)? **Functional API**, the recommended default.
3. Does a *piece* of it need custom computation? Write that piece as a **subclassed layer** and use it inside the Functional model.
4. Does the overall forward pass need loops, recursion or other non-DAG logic? Then use **Model subclassing**, and accept the loss of connectivity tooling.

deeper.title: Parameter counts for Listing 7.15
deeper.body:
Using the Dense rule params = inputs × units + units:

- Dense(64) on 3 features: $3\cdot 64 + 64 = 256$
- Classifier(num_classes=10) = Dense(10) on 64 features: $64\cdot 10 + 10 = 650$
- Total: **906** trainable parameters.

With `Classifier(num_classes=2)` instead, the head would be Dense(1, sigmoid): $64 + 1 = 65$ parameters.

deeper.title: Why one sigmoid unit for two classes
deeper.body: Beyond the book: a 2-way softmax over logits $(z_0, z_1)$ gives $p_1 = \frac{e^{z_1}}{e^{z_0}+e^{z_1}} = \sigma(z_1 - z_0)$. Only the difference of the logits matters, so a single unit producing $z = z_1 - z_0$ followed by a sigmoid expresses the same family of classifiers with half the output weights. That is why `Classifier` picks `num_units = 1` with `"sigmoid"` when `num_classes == 2`.

misconceptions.claim: Subclassing is the 'professional' choice and should be preferred.
misconceptions.correction: The authors recommend the Functional API whenever the model can be expressed as a DAG of layers, because it keeps layer connectivity for plotting and feature extraction.

misconceptions.claim: A Functional model cannot be called inside another model's call().
misconceptions.correction: It can, as Listing 7.16 shows. Functional models are Layers.

misconceptions.claim: Binary classification requires a 2-unit softmax output.
misconceptions.correction: Classifier uses 1 sigmoid unit when num_classes == 2, which is the standard and equivalent choice.
In Listing 7.16 num_classes isn't used. The classifier is always the binary Functional model.

takeaways: A subclassed model can be called on symbolic tensors inside a Functional model (Listing 7.15).
A Functional model can be assigned as an attribute and called inside a subclassed model's call() (Listing 7.16).
Classifier picks 1 sigmoid unit for 2 classes and num_classes softmax units otherwise.
Choose the API that fits the job. If the model is a DAG of layers, prefer the Functional API.
The Functional API's advantage is direct access to layer connectivity, used for plotting and feature extraction.

questions.question: What output layer does Classifier(num_classes=2) create?
questions.explanation: The if-branch sets num_units = 1 and activation = "sigmoid" when num_classes == 2. A 2-unit softmax would be the else-branch only for num_classes=2, which the code avoids. A 2-unit sigmoid is multi-label. A 1-unit softmax always outputs 1.0.

questions.question: How many trainable parameters does the Functional model at the end of Listing 7.15 have?
questions.answer: 906 (256 in Dense(64) on 3 inputs + 650 in the 10-unit softmax Classifier).

questions.question: What criterion do the authors give for choosing the Functional API over model subclassing?
questions.answer: If the model can be expressed as a directed acyclic graph of layers, use the Functional API.
questions.explanation: It offers a good ease-of-use/flexibility trade-off and keeps layer connectivity for plotting and feature extraction.

questions.question: In Listing 7.16, how is the Functional model binary_classifier used?
options: It is assigned as an attribute in __init__ and called inside call()
It is passed to compile() as a loss
questions.answer: It is assigned as an attribute in __init__ and called inside call()
questions.explanation: self.classifier = binary_classifier, then return self.classifier(features). MyModel subclasses keras.Model, not binary_classifier. It isn't a loss, and call() is still MyModel's own method.

questions.question: Why does Listing 7.16 work even though MyModel never specifies an input shape?
questions.answer: MyModel creates its weights when it is first called on data (p.227). Dense(64) adapts to whatever input size it sees, and its 64-wide output matches binary_classifier's Input(shape=(64,)).
questions.explanation: Subclassed models build lazily, and the Functional sub-model only constrains its own input width.

questions.question: Which benefit of the Functional API is explicitly cited in section 7.2.5?
options: Direct access to layer connectivity for plotting and feature extraction
Support for recursion in the forward pass
questions.answer: Direct access to layer connectivity for plotting and feature extraction
questions.explanation: Stated in the second paragraph of 7.2.5. Speed isn't mentioned. Recursion is a subclassing capability (p.228). Tuning isn't discussed here.

questions.question: Could you write a Functional model that uses a custom subclassed layer for one step, and say why that's often the best of both worlds?
questions.answer: Yes. Define the layer as a subclass, call it on a symbolic tensor in the Functional graph, and the model keeps its connectivity while the custom logic stays local.
questions.explanation: This previews p.230: Functional models with subclassed layers give high flexibility while keeping the advantages of the Functional API.
